text: FREDERICTON, April 24, 1909. The Saint John River, swollen by a late thaw and three days of heavy rain, broke over its banks shortly after midnight, and by daylight the lower part of the city was under water. Merchants along Queen Street were carrying their stock to upper floors by lantern light. Water stood four feet deep at the railway freight sheds, and boats were plying streets where carriages ran the day before. Several families on the flats were taken off their roofs by men in canoes. No lives are reported lost, but the damage to cellars, lumber piles and the booms above the city is expected to be heavy.
label: flood

text: The Bow River rose 1.4 m overnight on May 9, 2007, after a burst of rapid snowmelt. Two campgrounds near Canmore were evacuated as a precaution; no injuries were reported.
label: flood

text: Brandon, Man., spring 1958. The Assiniboine crested eleven feet above normal on the morning of April 30 after a week of steady rise. Volunteers filled some 40,000 sandbags to shore up the dikes along the east end, but a section near the exhibition grounds gave way and water poured into about 120 homes. The army sent a detachment with pumps and amphibious vehicles to help move people out.
label: flood

text: Between 6 and 9 p.m. on July 22, 2011, a stalled line of thunderstorms dropped roughly 110 mm of rain on north Oshawa. Storm sewers could not keep up, sewage backed into basements across several subdivisions, and a culvert washout closed a stretch of Taunton Road. The city logged more than 1,800 calls about flooded basements over the following two days.
label: flood

text: Ice jam at the mouth of the Petitcodiac, March 1913. When the river ice began to move on the afternoon of the 18th, it grounded on the flats below Moncton and the water backed up behind it faster than anyone expected. By evening the marsh roads were under three feet of water, several barns were flooded to the mangers and a number of cattle drowned in their stalls. Farmers spent the night ferrying stock to the uplands on rafts made of fence rails.
label: flood

text: Photograph, item 14 in the collection. Main Street, Grand Forks, B.C., looking east, June 1961. The Kettle River had come up through the storm drains the night before and stood about two feet deep in the business district. Note the plank walkway laid along the store fronts and the rowboat tied to the hotel verandah. According to the donor's note on the back, the family lost their piano and most of the winter's preserves in the cellar, and the school stayed closed for nine days while the town dried out.
label: flood

text: Situation report no. 3, Town of Peace River, 0800 hrs, 6 May 2008. River level at the town gauge is 9.2 m and holding steady after the ice run passed overnight. Approximately 140 residents of the low-lying west end remain under an evacuation order. Sandbag barriers along 100 Street held; minor seepage reported at two locations. Public Works continues pumping. Boil-water advisory remains in effect.
label: flood

text: Spring runoff, 1964: the Red Deer River topped its banks at Drumheller on April 19 and spread across the lower end of the valley. Some thirty families moved out until the water dropped.
label: flood

text: HEAVY RAINS WASH OUT RAILWAY LINE. Kamloops, June 3, 1921. For the third time this spring the North Thompson has gone on a rampage, and this time the damage is worse than any in living memory along the valley. Ranchers at Louis Creek report hay meadows two feet under water and fences carried away for miles. A bridge on the wagon road below Barriere was lifted bodily off its piers and now lies against a gravel bar. Section crews are working day and night to repair three washouts on the grade, and no trains have passed since Tuesday. A rancher named Whitlock is missing; his team was found drowned in a slough near the river.
label: flood

text: Shortly before 4 a.m. on May 28, 1999, a thirty-metre section of the earthen dyke protecting the Glen Valley area of Langley gave way under pressure from the swollen Fraser. Floodwaters spread across roughly 600 hectares of farmland within hours. Dairy herds were walked to higher ground with the help of neighbours and municipal crews, and 45 households were evacuated. Losses to crops, fencing and outbuildings were later put at $6 million.
label: flood

text: From the diary of Mrs. E. Hall, Portage la Prairie, 12 April 1904: River came up in the night and we are surrounded. Henry took the cow to the Fergusons' in the wagon with the water to the axles. Bread is wet.
label: flood

text: BELLEVILLE, March 27, 1961. Torrential rains over the weekend sent the Moira River surging through the city yesterday, flooding more than 200 cellars in the downtown area and forcing the closing of the Front Street bridge. City engineers said the river rose nearly six feet in twenty hours. Firemen pumped out the basement of the general hospital, where water threatened the boiler room.
label: flood

text: Flash flood, Highway 3 east of Hope, 14 Nov 2009: debris-laden runoff plugged and then blew out two culverts. Road closed 36 hours.
label: flood

text: Overland flooding, Rural Municipality of Rhineland, spring 1987. A deep snowpack and a rapid warm-up in the third week of April produced runoff that the frozen ground could not absorb. Drainage ditches filled within days, and sheets of water moved north across the fields toward the Red, cutting off farmsteads and turning several provincial roads into causeways. Ring dikes held around Altona and Plum Coulee, but at least 35 farmyards were flooded and some 70 people left their homes for a week or longer. The province opened a claims office in Winkler and paid disaster assistance for damaged wells, septic fields and stored grain.
label: flood

text: An unusually high spring tide, coming on top of a freshet in the rivers, broke through an aboiteau on the Tantramar marshes in March 1917. Several hundred acres of hayland were soaked with salt water and are expected to be of little use for some seasons.
label: flood

text: Woodstock, N.B., April 1953. When the ice let go above Hartland early Sunday, it piled up again at the bend below town and the river rose eight feet in under three hours. Lower Main Street was flooded to the window sills, and the water plant shut down when its pumps went under. Residents were told to boil drinking water. The jam held until Tuesday afternoon, then broke free with a roar heard across town.
label: flood

text: Basement flooding complaints: 412 received between 18:00 and 23:59 following 74 mm of rainfall. Wards 3, 5 and 9 most affected. Sewer backflow suspected at the Ellis Avenue pumping station. City of Guelph, 2 July 2005.
label: flood

text: Sir, I have the honour to report that Swift Current Creek rose between the 8th and 12th instant to a height not seen by any settler in the district. The low part of the town and the brick yard were under water, and some fifty persons were taken by boat to the railway station and the school. A man named Ostrander drowned while trying to save a raft of lumber. I attended with two constables and assisted the town authorities in patrolling the flooded streets at night. The water has since fallen about three feet. (Report, R.N.W.M.P. Swift Current detachment, June 1911)
label: flood

text: High water on Okanagan Lake through June 1990 flooded lakeshore properties from Vernon to Penticton. The lake peaked roughly half a metre above full pool after a heavy snowpack melted late and fast. Homeowners stacked sandbags along the beaches, docks floated free, and several low-lying parks were closed. On windy days, waves chewed away at the soft shoreline.
label: flood

text: Floodwaters from the Thames inundated the low-lying west end of London, Ont., in late March 1960, driving about 150 families from their homes. A sudden thaw had melted a heavy snowpack in three days, and rain on the 28th finished the job. Water stood waist-deep on several streets near the forks, and the utilities commission cut the gas to flooded blocks. Families were billeted with relatives or in a school gymnasium until the river fell back.
label: flood

text: The remnants of a tropical storm stalled over the Annapolis Valley on the night of 21 August 1988, and rain fell in sheets for fourteen hours. Totals of 150 to 200 mm sent the Cornwallis River and dozens of small brooks over their banks. In Kentville the river spread across the flats behind the main street and filled basements and parking lots; upstream, a mill pond dam gave way and the surge carried a barn into the river. Roads were washed out in at least thirty places and the province closed several secondary highways. About 260 people spent the night in shelters, and farmers lost much of the late vegetable crop to silt and standing water.
label: flood

text: The Grand River rose suddenly at Galt on the 2nd, carrying away a footbridge and flooding the mills along the waterfront. The ice had gone out upstream during the night, and by morning the water was over the mill races and into the lower floors of two woollen mills, where several hundred hands were sent home. Merchants on the main street hoisted their goods onto the counters. The flood went down nearly as quickly as it came. March 1912.
label: flood

text: Minutes of a special meeting of council, Town of Estevan, 25 April 1969. Present: the Mayor and five councillors. The Town Engineer reported that the Souris River had risen above the culverts at the south end and that water was entering homes on River Street. Moved and seconded that the Town hire two front-end loaders, purchase 5,000 sandbags, and open the arena as a reception centre for flooded-out families. Carried.
label: flood

text: Breakup on the Yukon River came early and violently at Carmacks in May 1989. A jam formed downstream of the village on the evening of the 11th, and within two hours water had backed up over the bank and into the lower part of the community. Ice slabs the size of cars were shoved onto the road and against the walls of several cabins. Residents moved elders and children to the school on the hill, and the territorial government flew in an emergency coordinator, pumps and bottled water. By morning the jam had released and the water dropped quickly, leaving silt and broken ice through yards and the campground. Fourteen homes were damaged, two beyond repair, and every well was tested before families were allowed back.
label: flood

text: Freshet flows on the Similkameen washed out a section of the Princeton to Hedley road on 30 May 2002. A detour is in place.
label: flood

text: RENFREW, May 7, 1928. The Bonnechere is higher than it has been in twenty years and the water is lapping at the deck of the Raglan Street bridge. Several cellars on the low side of town are flooded and the electric light plant has been shut down. Rain continues.
label: flood

text: It was the kind of rain old-timers in Sussex said they had never seen: close to five inches between supper and midnight on August 14, 1955, falling on ground already soaked by a wet week. Trout Creek and the Kennebecasis came up together, and by two in the morning water was running through the hotel lobby and over the tracks at the station. Firemen went door to door on Main Street with flashlights, waking families on the low side and carrying children through knee-deep water. A dairy farmer lost forty head when his pasture went under. When the creek dropped, residents found cars wedged against the bridge railings and a layer of red mud on every floor.
label: flood

text: Spring runoff flooded part of Maple Creek, Sask., in April 1952; about 80 residents moved out for several days. The creek, swollen by meltwater from the Cypress Hills, overflowed into the east end and ran through yards and basements. The town opened the curling rink for evacuees, and ranchers with trucks helped move furniture. Damage was mostly to cellars, fences and stored feed.
label: flood

text: The Township of Tay Valley declared a state of emergency on April 17, 2014, after heavy rain on top of a late snowpack pushed lake and river levels to record highs. Several cottage roads are under water and some residents can reach their homes only by boat. Free sand and bags are available at the township garage. Residents are reminded not to drive through flooded roads and to check on their neighbours.
label: flood

text: Old residents of Souris, Man., long spoke of the spring of 1907, when the river that gave the town its name came up faster than anyone could remember. A heavy winter's snow went off in a week of warm wind and rain, and on the night of April 19 the water rose over the low end of town, carrying ice cakes into yards and against the walls of the mill. A footbridge was torn loose and swept downstream. Families took refuge in the Methodist church and the upper storeys of the hotel, while a few men stayed out in boats to save livestock. In the weeks after the water went down, wells were fouled and several cases of typhoid were reported, which the doctor blamed on flooded privies.
label: flood

text: Overland flooding closed Highway 39 near Milestone, Sask., for three days in April 2001. Crews placed temporary culverts to drain water ponded against the road grade.
label: flood

text: A sudden thaw and two days of rain sent the Humber River over its banks below Deer Lake in March 1967, flooding the road to Corner Brook and several homes at Pasadena. Families were taken out by dory, and the highway was closed for most of a week while crews rebuilt the washed-out shoulders.
label: flood

text: After-action review, Sault Ste. Marie flash flood of 17 August 2006. Summary: an intense thunderstorm produced 90 to 120 mm of rain over the east end in roughly two hours. Findings: (1) the storm sewer network was overwhelmed within forty minutes; (2) a blocked culvert diverted a creek across two residential streets; (3) the emergency operations centre was activated late because the forecast underestimated rainfall. Impacts included about 900 flooded basements, one road collapse and the temporary closure of the ground floor of a long-term care home. Recommendations: backwater valve subsidies, culvert inspections before each summer, and earlier activation thresholds.
label: flood

text: Kettle Creek overflowed at St. Thomas in the spring of 1925; several small houses on the flats floated off their foundations and the lower bridge was impassable for days. The creek rose after two days of warm rain on deep snow, and the water came up so quickly in the night that some families escaped in their nightclothes. One house came to rest against the railway trestle.
label: flood

text: WATER STILL RISING AT CHATHAM. The Thames is out of its banks for the second time this month, and the King Street merchants have given up trying to keep it out of their cellars. Teams are hauling goods to higher ground. February 1938.
label: flood

text: Hydrometric note, Whitemud River near Westbourne, 1974 season: peak instantaneous discharge occurred on 22 April, roughly three times the long-term mean annual peak. Flow left the channel at several points and ponded on adjacent farmland for two to three weeks, delaying seeding across an estimated 4,000 acres.
label: flood

text: Flash flood in the Crowsnest Pass: a cloudburst over the mountains on the afternoon of July 9, 1931, sent a wall of muddy water down a creek into the mining town of Coleman. Houses near the creek were filled to the windows, the main road was torn up, and two children were swept off their feet but pulled out alive by a miner. The coal company lent men and teams to clear the streets.
label: flood

text: Sandbagging continues around the clock in Selkirk as the Red River ice jam north of the bridge holds. More than 300 volunteers, many of them high school students, have placed an estimated 60,000 bags since Friday. Water has entered about 25 homes. (Selkirk, Man., April 1983)
label: flood

text: It took the river less than a day to undo forty years of work. On 4 May 1973, the Saint John at Maugerville came up through the fields and over the old road, and by noon the only way in or out was by boat. Neighbours went from farm to farm in outboard skiffs, moving hens, feed and furniture into lofts. Cattle were swum across to the high ground behind the church. The water stayed for eleven days. When it left, it took fences, woodpiles and the topsoil of more than one garden, and it left behind a smell that people said lasted all summer.
label: flood

text: Washout. A torrent from heavy rain undermined the township road at the 6th concession; a car went into the gap at night, no injuries. Grey County, June 1983.
label: flood
